title: Article 303 — Restrictions on the legislative powers of the Union and of the States with regard to trade and commerce

content.overview: Article 303 provides that neither Parliament nor the Legislature of a State shall have power to make any law giving, or authorising the giving of, any preference to one State over another, or making or authorising the making of any discrimination between one State and another, by virtue of any entry relating to trade and commerce in any of the Lists in the Seventh Schedule. Exception: Parliament may discriminate or prefer if it is declared that it is necessary to do so for the purpose of dealing with a situation arising from scarcity of goods in any part of India.
content.glance: No Union or State law may prefer or discriminate between States on trade/commerce entries — except Parliament may do so if declared necessary to deal with scarcity of goods in any part of India.
content.study:
Article 303 anti-preference / anti-discrimination rule:
(1) General bar: neither Parliament nor State Legislatures may by law give preference to one State over another or discriminate between States, by virtue of trade and commerce entries in the Seventh Schedule.
(2) Exception: Parliament may, if it is declared that it is necessary to deal with a situation arising from scarcity of goods in any part of India.

Examination: no preference/discrimination between States; scarcity exception for Parliament only; link Arts 301–304.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. No Union or State law preferring or discriminating between States under trade/commerce entries.
2. Exception: Parliament may prefer/discriminate if declared necessary to deal with scarcity of goods in any part of India.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 303 prohibit?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 303 provides that neither Parliament nor a State Legislature shall have power to make any law giving preference to one State over another or discriminating between one State and another by virtue of any entry relating to trade and commerce in the Seventh Schedule. Parliament may, however, do so if it is declared that it is necessary to deal with a situation arising from scarcity of goods in any part of India.

examTips: No inter-State preference/discrimination; scarcity exception for Parliament.

keyTakeaways: Art 303: bar on inter-State preference/discrimination in trade laws; scarcity exception.
